<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914548_theRebbe_632" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914548_theRebbe_632__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The purpose of man's creation is that he be upright, and the concept of teshuvah applies even to completely righteous individuals, as the soul's descent itself is a form of exile requiring return.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the intention in the creation of man is that it should be in the manner of "God made man upright"35,</t>
    <t s="2">that he should go all his days on the straight path,</t>
    <t s="3">according to the precise language of our Sages, of blessed memory36,</t>
    <t s="4">"Whom did He consult? With the souls of the righteous."</t>
    <t s="5">Specifically "righteous"37.</t>
    <t s="6">And even though "in the place where penitents stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand,"</t>
    <t s="7">it is known38</t>
    <t s="8">that the concept of teshuvah is</t>
    <t s="9">(not only regarding sins,</t>
    <t s="10">but also)</t>
    <t s="11">the return of the soul to its source and root,</t>
    <t s="12">and this teshuvah applies even to completely righteous individuals.</t>
    <t s="13">For the very fact that his soul is found below and not in its source and root,</t>
    <t s="14">which is its true place</t>
    <t s="15">[and particularly that the soul being below in this physical world</t>
    <t s="16">is "a state of actual exile"39],</t>
    <t s="17">requires that it be returned to its place.</t>
    <t s="18">And the superiority of penitents over completely righteous individuals,</t>
    <t s="19">that "in the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous cannot stand,"</t>
    <t s="20">applies also to this teshuvah</t>
    <t s="21">(of the righteous).</t>
    <t s="22">And the ultimate purpose of the soul's descent into this physical world is for the sake of this teshuvah40.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The three superior levels of penitents over the completely righteous also apply to the soul that becomes a penitent through its descent, as the distance of descent arouses great thirst and the subsequent closeness brings immense delight.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">The explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">that the three aforementioned superior levels of penitents over completely righteous individuals</t>
    <t s="2">also apply to the soul when it becomes a penitent through its descent below, relative to how it was before the descent</t>
    <t s="3">(the level of "righteous").</t>
    <t s="4">For since even the distance caused by the soul's descent below</t>
    <t s="5">(even when one has never transgressed)</t>
    <t s="6">is an immense distance,</t>
    <t s="7">to the extent that the descent below is "a state of actual exile"</t>
    <t s="8">(as above),</t>
    <t s="9">this distance arouses in him a great thirst,</t>
    <t s="10">and also the delight and joy of the closeness after the distance is a very great delight.</t>
    <t s="11">And likewise regarding the aspect of novelty in teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="12">for since the concept of teshuvah</t>
    <t s="13">(even the teshuvah of the righteous)</t>
    <t s="14">is that he becomes embittered over his state</t>
    <t s="15">(that he is distant from Divinity)41</t>
    <t s="16">and wants to exit his state and his existence42,</t>
    <t s="17">it is therefore43,</t>
    <t s="18">this is a matter of novelty.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Nevertheless, the primary superiority of penitents is in the aspect of novelty, which applies most fully to literal penitents, as for the righteous the desire to fulfill God's will already includes the self-nullification of teshuvah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">However, nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="1">since it can be said that this statement of our Sages does not depart from its simple meaning,</t>
    <t s="2">this that they said "in the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous cannot stand"</t>
    <t s="3">is primarily regarding penitents in their simple sense44.</t>
    <t s="4">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that this primary superiority of penitents being in penitents in their simple sense</t>
    <t s="6">is regarding the superiority of the novelty in teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="7">For regarding the superiority of thirst,</t>
    <t s="8">and regarding the superiority of closeness after distance,</t>
    <t s="9">there is no difference</t>
    <t s="10">(so much)</t>
    <t s="11">between them,</t>
    <t s="12">and this that the primary elevation of teshuvah is in simple teshuvah is regarding the superiority of the novelty in teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="13">The explanation is,</t>
    <t s="14">that regarding the righteous,</t>
    <t s="15">since their soul shines within them in revelation,</t>
    <t s="16">their bitterness over their distance from Divinity,</t>
    <t s="17">to the point that the bitterness touches the soul,</t>
    <t s="18">is not so wondrous or novel</t>
    <t s="19">(so much).</t>
    <t s="20">And although the concept of teshuvah is that he exits his own existence,</t>
    <t s="21">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="22">since the soul by its nature desires to fulfill the will of its Master,</t>
    <t s="23">and the intention from Above</t>
    <t s="24">(the will of its Master)</t>
    <t s="25">in the soul's descent into the body is to come to teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="26">therefore in the desire</t>
    <t s="27">(that stems from the nature of the soul)</t>
    <t s="28">to fulfill the will of its Master,</t>
    <t s="29">is also included the exiting from his existence that comes through teshuvah45.</t>
    <t s="30">Not so regarding simple teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="31">since beforehand</t>
    <t s="32">(before the teshuvah)</t>
    <t s="33">he was in a state where he did not do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He46,</t>
    <t s="34">for he committed sins intentionally,</t>
    <t s="35">this that he later does teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="36">is not a continuation of his previous state,</t>
    <t s="37">and through teshuvah he becomes an entirely new existence.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
